title: Asking questions in Spanish
examples: How do I ask 'Where is the station?' in Spanish?
What are the question words in Spanish?
Can you show me how to use ¿Por qué?

explain.say: Today we learn to ask questions in Spanish.
To ask what something is, we use ¿Qué?. For example, ¿Qué es esto?
If you want to know a person, you ask ¿Quién?. For instance, ¿Quién es tu amigo?

draw.text: ¿Quién es tu amigo? (Who is your friend?)

explain.say: To find a place, you ask ¿Dónde?. For example, ¿Dónde está el baño?

draw.text: ¿Dónde está el baño? (Where is the bathroom?)

explain.say: We also ask about time with ¿Cuándo? and reason with ¿Por qué?. For example, ¿Cuándo es la fiesta?

draw.text: ¿Cuándo es la fiesta? (When is the party?)

explain.say: In real life, if you are lost, you can ask a local person. You can point and ask, ¿Dónde está la estación de tren?

faq.q: Do I need to change the word order when I ask a question?
faq.a: Yes, the question word usually comes at the very beginning. You must also remember the inverted question marks.
asks: What goes first in a Spanish question?
Is the word order different for questions?

faq.q: When do I use ¿Por qué? versus ¿Por qué razón?
faq.a: Use ¿Por qué? when you want to know the reason. It is often followed by 'porque' in the answer.
asks: What is the difference between ¿Por qué? and por qué?

faq.q: Do all question words need an accent mark?
faq.a: Yes, the main question words like ¿Qué?, ¿Quién?, ¿Dónde?, ¿Cuándo?, and ¿Por qué? always need an accent mark.

faq.q: What are the question words for 'How' or 'How many'?
faq.a: The word for 'How' is ¿Cómo? and for 'How many' is ¿Cuántos?/¿Cuántas? You must match the noun gender.
asks: How do I ask 'How are you?'

faq.q: Do I need to put question marks at the end of every question?
faq.a: Yes, in Spanish, you must use both an opening ¿ and a closing ? mark. This is very important.
asks: Where do the question marks go?
Do I write ¿ at the start?

facts: Spanish questions always start with an opening question mark: ¿.
The main question words are ¿Qué?, ¿Quién?, ¿Dónde?, ¿Cuándo?, and ¿Por qué?.
When asking a question, the question word usually comes at the beginning.
The word ¿Por qué? is used to ask 'Why?'

quiz.say: Turn this statement into a question: 'Ella es mi hermana.'
quiz.why: You are asking about the person, so you use ¿Quién? at the beginning.

wrong.0: This asks 'When is she?', which refers to time, not identity.
wrong.2: This asks 'What is she?', which is incorrect for a person.
wrong.3: This asks 'Where is she?', which is a place, not a person.

quiz.say: Turn this statement into a question: 'El libro está en la mesa.'
quiz.why: Since you are asking for the location of the book, you correctly use ¿Dónde?.

wrong.0: This asks 'When is the book?', which relates to time, not place.
wrong.2: This asks 'What is on the table?', but the question word should focus on location.
wrong.3: This asks 'Who is on the table?', but the book is an object, not a person.

quiz.say: How do you ask 'Why is the party tomorrow?'
quiz.why: Because you are asking for the reason, you must use the word ¿Por qué? at the start.

wrong.1: This asks 'What is the party tomorrow?', confusing the reason with the object.
wrong.2: This asks 'When is the party?', which is a different question entirely.
wrong.3: This asks 'Where is the party?', confusing location with reason.
